title: Slim the /sdlc skill to run+report+HITL: three independent PRs — B (long-haul monitoring tooling), C (supervision cap-wall hardening), D (skill deletion gated on overseer coverage-map)
summary: Three mutually-independent units of work with three distinct risk profiles. PR B (additive/low): add client-side --exclude-types/--quiet filtering flags to the pure-stdlib skills/sdlc/bin/wait-status launcher, and a new slice.closed EventType emitted at SliceScheduler.record_complete/record_failure via an injected emitter callback (mirroring the existing _hitl_escalator injection pattern), added to the _STATUS_WAIT_EVENT_TYPES allowlist so it reaches /status/wait consumers. PR C (behavioral/medium-high, all in orchestrator/supervision_policy.py + JobSupervisor): detect the all-producers agent-invocation-failure streak signature carrying bare throttling wording (429 / 'rate limit' / 'overloaded' — the signatures auth_errors.py deliberately keeps OFF the EX_AUTH_FATAL path) and classify it as a NEW transient rate-limit class distinct from abnormal, so it does NOT hit the >=10 agent-invocation-fail-streak halt that currently exhausts in minutes because backoff caps at 30s (SUPERVISION_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS). On that class, perform a windowed paced retry across the rolling cap window (hours-scale) using a restart_phase-equivalent that PRESERVES landed slices, with a deterministic-loop guard that escalates instead of looping when a restart reproduces the identical failure at the same point; bounding follows the operator's cq-1 resolution — NO hard wall-clock ceiling, but emit an OVERSEER_ALERT once the wait crosses a threshold. PR D (deletion/medium, GATED): delete the five host-side detector blocks + Host detector migration (#1962) section + Overseer-Absent Fallback from skills/sdlc/SKILL.md and remove overseer_owns_host_detection entirely — but ONLY after a coverage-map positively identifies, per deleted block, a concrete overseer OVERSEER_ALERT emitter the skill already surfaces. The naive 'the overseer already does this' assumption does NOT hold uniformly: the live overseer monitor emits a DIFFERENT deterministic vocab (post_consensus_stall, incomplete_consensus_stall, rerun_anomaly, status_inconsistency, hitl_propagation_failure, cross_phase_inconsistency, orchestrator_unreachable) while the host vocab (agent-stall/agent-silent/agent-nack-unresolved/phase-long-running) exists in production ONLY as a dedup signature map in shared/egg_overseer/state.py and is otherwise produced via the overseer's Haiku classifier/adjudicator (LLM path), not a deterministic threshold detector. Any block whose parity cannot be confirmed is a HITL at the point of discovery, not a silent delete.

problem_statement.description: A long, failure-rich 19-slice run (#3312) surfaced monitoring + recovery behavior that kept it alive; the original impulse was to codify that playbook into skills/sdlc/SKILL.md. That is the wrong home. The skill's job is narrow — run pipelines, keep the user updated, broker HITL decisions + surface overseer escalations. Detection, classification, and recovery belong in the orchestrator + overseer, which have in-pod liveness and own the pipeline state machine, and there they protect EVERY pipeline, not just an attended /sdlc session. This pipeline delivers the three remaining independent PRs (B, C, D); PR A (#3421 consensus-timeout Retry->restart_phase) already landed and is out of scope.
problem_statement.grounded_against_tree: 2026-07-06; branch egg/issue-3364-architect/work. Refiner facts re-verified live against the current tree: wait-status arg parser (only --since/--inner-timeout/--max-iterations at 293/301/310, json line printing at 249/271), supervision_policy.py:18-19 (BACKOFF_FACTOR=2, CAP_SECONDS=30) + streak anomaly 25-26, auth_errors.py:24-28/45-47 (throttling signatures intentionally absent from _AUTH_FATAL_PATTERNS), slice_scheduler.py record_complete:361 / record_failure:371 (neither emits an event today) + existing _hitl_escalator Callable injection at 159/180, _STATUS_WAIT_EVENT_TYPES at orchestrator/routes/pipelines/__init__.py:405 (checked at _routes_status.py:349), EventType enum at orchestrator/events.py:35, overseer_owns_host_detection at orchestrator/models/_config.py:388 (default False) read at _routes_status.py:126-127, overseer emitters via _broadcast_alert in orchestrator/overseer/monitor/_anomaly_checks.py + _consensus_stall.py, and the agent-* host vocab present in production ONLY at shared/egg_overseer/state.py:86 as a last-alert dedup map.

JSON lines are printed to stdout at :249 and :271 (print(json.dumps(line), flush=True)) — these are the two client-side chokepoints where --exclude-types drop + --quiet suppression must apply. Keep the launcher self-contained (no new imports/deps).
orchestrator/events.py: class EventType(StrEnum) at :35. Members are dotted string values grouped by domain (pipeline.*, phase.*, agent.*, consensus.*, decision.*, progress.*, system.health_check.*). A new SLICE_CLOSED = 'slice.closed' member belongs here; no slice.* member exists yet (grounded).
orchestrator/slice_scheduler.py: record_complete(slice_id) at :361 sets state=COMPLETE, completed_at, and calls _unblock_children — emits NO event today.
record_failure(slice_id) at :371 sets state=FAILED, failed_at, arms cascade timer — emits NO event today.

The scheduler ALREADY carries an injected callback for out-of-band signalling: _hitl_escalator: Callable[[str,str], None] | None injected in __init__ (:159, stored :180) and invoked AFTER the lock is released (:352-354). This is the canonical injection seam for a slice.closed emitter — mirror it (a Callable emitter injected at construction, invoked outside the lock in both record_complete and record_failure).
orchestrator/routes/pipelines: _STATUS_WAIT_EVENT_TYPES frozenset defined at __init__.py:405; the /status/wait filter checks event.event_type.value against it at _routes_status.py:349. slice.closed must be ADDED to this allowlist or it will be dropped before reaching wait-status consumers.

shared/egg_agent/auth_errors.py: EX_AUTH_FATAL=77 (:40); _AUTH_FATAL_PATTERNS (:47). Docstring :24-28 + comment :45-47 make explicit that transient throttling (HTTP 429 / 'rate limit' / 'overloaded') is INTENTIONALLY absent from the fatal patterns — these stay on the normal backoff-and-respawn path. A matched weekly/usage cap message DOES route to EX_AUTH_FATAL on its own wording; a bare 429/'overloaded' cap wall does NOT and falls through to the abnormal path. PR C keys off exactly the bare-throttling signatures this file excludes.
orchestrator/supervision_policy.py: SUPERVISION_BACKOFF_FACTOR=2 (:18), SUPERVISION_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS=30 (:19): linear streak*factor backoff capped at 30s. Streak anomaly agent-invocation-fail-streak (:25-26) fires a sticky halt at the >=10 threshold — so a persistent cap wall exhausts in minutes.
This is the module that owns classification (abnormal vs. the streak anomaly) and backoff; the new transient rate-limit class + windowed pacing live here / in JobSupervisor.
orchestrator/concurrent_executor.py: Failure-streak exhaustion is broadcast at :988 (refiner anchor) — the all-producers signature (every producer failing on the same throttling wording) is observable at/around this streak-tracking site; that signature is what distinguishes a cap wall from a genuine per-agent abnormal failure.
pr_c_supervision.cq-1 resolution (binding): Retry until the cap lifts with NO hard wall-clock ceiling, BUT emit an OVERSEER_ALERT once the wait crosses a threshold so an attended operator is informed while auto-recovery continues. The paced-retry loop is unbounded in wall-clock; the observability escape hatch is the threshold alert (not a halt).

skills/sdlc/SKILL.md: 1600 lines. Delete: 'Host detector migration (issue #1962)' section (~553); 'Overseer-Absent Fallback' (~573); the five host-side detector blocks — Stall detection (~637), Silent agent detection (~644), NACK escalation (~679), Long-Running Phase Detection (~722), and the host-side detection TRIGGER of Stuck Pipeline Rescue (~750, workflow itself STAYS); plus the short-flow Stall detection block (~1517). run_migrated_detectors named at ~555 exists in SKILL.md prose ONLY (no production symbol).

PRESERVE (AC-D3, critical): the render-on-OVERSEER_ALERT paths — the Long-Running Implement Phase AskUserQuestion flow and the Unresolved NACK AskUserQuestion flow must still fire when the matching OVERSEER_ALERT arrives. Removing host-side DETECTION must not remove alert-driven RENDERING.

PRESERVE (AC-D4/AC-D5): arg parse/seed, pre-refine triage, submit, the Monitor wait-status loop (render + cursor threading), HITL brokering (phase_gate/choice/feedback, two-wave surfacing, cq-N/feedback-N), OVERSEER_ALERT surfacing, the user-initiated Stuck Pipeline Rescue workflow (Steps 1-3, minus its host-side detection trigger), and a short last-resort debugging section with two thin backstops (never blind-action a destructive recommendation — route through AskUserQuestion; TaskStop the Monitor before re-arming).
overseer_owns_host_detection: Declared orchestrator/models/_config.py:388 (bool Field, default False). Read at orchestrator/routes/pipelines/_routes_status.py:126-127 (getattr, into the status payload). Only these two production references. AC-D2: REMOVE the field + both references entirely (conclude the calibration window; do not flip the default). grep must be clean of the symbol afterward.
overseer emitter reality (the reason the: Live overseer monitor emitters (deterministic, structural): _anomaly_checks.py — orchestrator_unreachable (:102), rerun_anomaly (:167), status_inconsistency (:217), hitl_propagation_failure (:279), cross_phase_inconsistency (:360); _consensus_stall.py — post_consensus_stall (:137), incomplete_consensus_stall (:382). These are a DIFFERENT vocabulary from the host blocks.

The host vocab (agent-stall, agent-silent, agent-nack-unresolved, phase-long-running) appears in production ONLY at shared/egg_overseer/state.py:86 as an anomaly-type -> last-alert-datetime dedup map — NOT as an emitter. Agent-level classification into that vocab runs through the overseer Haiku classifier/adjudicator (LLM path), not a deterministic threshold. => For each deleted host block the coverage-map must name a concrete emitter (structural _broadcast_alert OR the classifier path) whose OVERSEER_ALERT the skill already surfaces; a block with no confirmed emitter is a HITL, not a silent delete into a dark gap.

findings.finding: B, C, D are genuinely independent — file-disjoint surfaces (wait-status/events/scheduler/status-route vs. supervision_policy/JobSupervisor vs. SKILL.md/_config/status-route). They should be three separate slices with no cross-blocking edges, EXCEPT PR D's internal gate (coverage-map before deletion). Note a soft overlap: both PR B and PR D touch orchestrator/routes/pipelines/_routes_status.py (B adds slice.closed to the allowlist which is defined in __init__.py, D removes the overseer_owns_host_detection getattr at :126-127) — different regions of a split package, but the planner should flag it so reviewers watch for a merge seam if the slices land concurrently.

PR B slice.closed should be emitted through an INJECTED emitter callback, mirroring the existing _hitl_escalator Callable seam (injected in __init__, invoked outside the scheduler lock). Emitting inside the lock risks re-entrancy/deadlock; the existing escalator deliberately fires post-lock-release. The payload must distinguish success vs failure and identify the slice (AC-B3) — record_complete carries slice_id + COMPLETE, record_failure carries slice_id + FAILED; a single event type with an outcome field is cleaner than two event types.

PR C's hardest architectural line is the transient-vs-deterministic distinction (AC-C4). The all-producers throttling-streak signature is the transient discriminator (every producer failing on 429/rate-limit/overloaded wording => cap wall, not code bug). The loop guard needs a stable notion of 'identical failure at the same point' — same failure signature AND same phase/slice progression across a restart. Preserving landed slices (AC-C3) means the restart_phase-equivalent must NOT reset completed slice runtimes; it re-arms only the in-flight/failed frontier. This is the medium-high risk area and warrants the heaviest test coverage.

cq-1 is resolved: unbounded paced retry with a threshold OVERSEER_ALERT. This means PR C must NOT introduce a hard halt on wall-clock elapse — the only escalation on a persistent cap is (a) the threshold alert (attended-operator visibility) and (b) the deterministic-loop guard (which escalates on IDENTICAL reproduction, a different trigger than 'been waiting too long'). The planner must not conflate the loop-guard escalation with a time-ceiling halt; they are orthogonal.

PR D's coverage-map is a real verification task, not a rubber stamp, and MUST be a task that precedes any SKILL.md deletion in the same slice's DAG. The five host blocks map to a MIX of deterministic overseer emitters (stall -> post_consensus_stall/incomplete_consensus_stall structural checks) and LLM-classifier paths (silent/nack/long-running -> Haiku classifier agent-* vocab). Where only the classifier path exists, parity is 'the overseer will classify and emit an OVERSEER_ALERT the skill surfaces' — the planner should require the coverage-map to state emitter + alert subject + which SKILL.md surface renders it, and to raise a HITL for any block that maps to nothing.

AC-D3 (preserve render-on-alert) is the highest-consequence regression risk in PR D: it is easy to over-delete and take out the AskUserQuestion flows that fire on Long-Running Implement Phase and Unresolved NACK alerts while removing their host-side detection. The deletion task must be scoped to detection/trigger prose only; a reviewer criterion should assert both render flows still fire on their alerts post-deletion.

overseer_owns_host_detection removal (AC-D2) is coupled to the SKILL.md deletion conceptually (both conclude the migration) but is a separate file surface (_config.py + _routes_status.py). It can be its own task within PR D's slice, sequenced AFTER the coverage-map (same gate rationale — do not remove the calibration flag until parity is confirmed). grep-clean of the symbol is the completion check.

design: wait-status: add --exclude-types (comma-separated) and --quiet to the parser (~:292-320); apply filtering at the two json.dumps print sites (:249, :271) — drop a line whose event type is in the exclude set, suppress non-essential lines under --quiet. Pure client-side; no new imports.
events.py: add SLICE_CLOSED = 'slice.closed' to EventType (:35 enum).

slice_scheduler.py: inject a slice-closed emitter Callable at __init__ (mirror _hitl_escalator: default None, stored, invoked OUTSIDE the lock). Call it from record_complete (:361) and record_failure (:371) with a payload carrying slice_id + outcome (complete|failed) so consumers distinguish success from failure.
routes/pipelines/__init__.py: add 'slice.closed' to _STATUS_WAIT_EVENT_TYPES (:405) so it passes the /status/wait allowlist checked at _routes_status.py:349.
Tests: two new flags (a filter that drops a type; --quiet); a slice completion AND a slice failure each emit exactly one allowlisted slice.closed.

Classification: detect the all-producers agent-invocation-failure streak whose underlying error carries bare throttling wording (429 / 'rate limit' / 'overloaded' — the signatures auth_errors.py excludes from EX_AUTH_FATAL). Introduce a distinct transient rate-limit classification so this signature does NOT feed the agent-invocation-fail-streak halt.

Windowed paced retry: on that classification, pace retries across the rolling cap window (hours-scale) rather than the 30s SUPERVISION_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS; do not hammer the API. Use a restart_phase-equivalent that PRESERVES landed slices (does not reset completed slice runtimes).

Deterministic-loop guard: capture a failure fingerprint (signature + phase/slice progression). If a restart reproduces the IDENTICAL fingerprint at the SAME point, stop and escalate (deterministic failure) instead of looping; if the restart advances state, continue.
Bounding per cq-1: no hard wall-clock ceiling; emit an OVERSEER_ALERT once the cumulative wait crosses a threshold (attended-operator visibility while auto-recovery continues).
Invariance guard (AC-C6): EX_AUTH_FATAL (incl. matched weekly/usage caps) and ordinary abnormal failures behave UNCHANGED — the new path triggers ONLY on the throttling-streak signature.

Tests: throttling-streak -> rate-limit classification (not abnormal); paced-retry pacing/window; landed-slice preservation across restart; loop-guard escalates on identical-failure reproduction vs. continues when the restart advances state; threshold OVERSEER_ALERT fires.
pr_c.risk: medium-high (live supervision behavior) — heaviest test coverage here

design: GATE FIRST (AC-D6): produce the coverage-map — for each of the five host blocks, name the concrete overseer emitter (structural _broadcast_alert subject OR the Haiku-classifier agent-* path) and the OVERSEER_ALERT subject the skill already surfaces. Record it in the plan/PR. Raise a HITL at the point of discovery for any block that maps to no emitter (do not delete into a dark gap).

Only after the map confirms parity: delete the Host detector migration (#1962) section, Overseer-Absent Fallback, and the five host-side detector blocks + the short-flow Stall block from SKILL.md — detection/trigger prose ONLY.

PRESERVE (AC-D3): the Long-Running Implement Phase and Unresolved NACK AskUserQuestion render-on-alert flows; the user-initiated Stuck Pipeline Rescue workflow (Steps 1-3) minus its host-side detection trigger; the two thin last-resort backstops.
Remove overseer_owns_host_detection entirely (AC-D2): the Field at _config.py:388 and both getattr references at _routes_status.py:126-127; grep-clean the symbol.
Tests/checks: grep-clean of deleted-block markers + overseer_owns_host_detection; assertion that both render-on-alert flows still fire on their OVERSEER_ALERTs.
pr_d.risk: medium (deletion, gated) — the render-on-alert preservation is the key regression surface

recommended_approach.sequencing: Three top-level independent slices (B, C, D) with no cross-blocking edges. Within PR D the coverage-map task MUST precede the SKILL.md deletion task and the overseer_owns_host_detection removal task (internal gate). C is the highest-risk slice; the planner should weight it toward test coverage of the classification + loop-guard + landed-slice preservation. Flag the soft _routes_status.py seam shared by B (allowlist) and D (flag removal) so concurrent landing is reviewed for a merge conflict, though they touch different regions.
